summary: Queue work instead of doing it all at once, spread across frames to avoid a hitch.
overview: Enqueue actions rather than running a big batch in one frame, and it drains a fixed number per frame. Good for spawning or initialising many objects, migrating a large save, or generating a big procedural grid. Not a singleton on purpose — add one per queue when you want separately paced budgets.
useCases: Spawning a large wave without a visible stall.
Rebuilding a big UI list a few rows per frame.
Running a one-off migration on load while the loading screen animates.

params.tuning: The whole tuning surface. Too low and a large queue takes visibly long; too high and you have reinvented the hitch.

gotchas.title: Work is spread, not made cheaper
gotchas.body: A thousand expensive actions still cost the same total. This buys a smooth frame rate, not less work.

gotchas.title: Order is preserved, completion time is not predictable
gotchas.body: Actions run in the order queued, but how long the queue takes depends on frame rate. Do not assume it finishes within a fixed number of seconds.
